decision.ratified_option: B — move the metadata write upstream; two-hash treatment only for watermark-enabled products
decision.canonical_statement: Embedded tempo/key/loop metadata is written once at ingest (14.08.03) into the stored master; it is a property of the product, not the buyer. Delivery therefore has at most one writer — the per-buyer forensic watermark, where enabled. Unmarked products are delivered byte-identical to the master, so the single published SHA-256 is correct as it stands. Watermark-enabled products keep the master's hash as the published build identity and add a per-grant SHA-256 of the bytes actually served, recorded at grant mint and auto-verified by the client; the panel shows both.

work_routed_onward.item: Per-grant SHA-256 over a stamped multi-GB stream (hash-and-trailer)
work_routed_onward.detail: A watermarked artifact's delivered bytes carry their own hash, which the client verifies. On a 100 GB library those bytes cannot be materialised twice, so the digest must be computed while serving and delivered at the end of the stream, and must survive resume since a grant's ranges are not one continuous read. Bounded to watermark-enabled products.

work_routed_onward.status: CHANGED — now settled rather than open
work_routed_onward.detail: The architecture stage receives a decided contract (master hash published; per-grant hash for marked artifacts only) instead of having to invent D-09's product promise.
The uncacheable set is now exactly the watermark-enabled inventory; the metadata write no longer sits on the delivery path. How large that set is depends on 14.03.05 Q-03.

work_routed_onward.item: Stored-artifact defect detection for marked inventory
work_routed_onward.detail: For a marked artifact the per-grant hash is derived from the master, so a corrupt master produces a matching per-grant hash and passes buyer-side verification. E-19 is no longer a universal backstop; ingest QA carries that load for marked inventory. Named in E-19.

master_mismatch.scope: unmarked artifacts — all software, large-format instruments, presets, MIDI, unwatermarked packs
master_mismatch.action: one automatic re-verify, then alert vendor and platform and QUARANTINE the build from new grants
master_mismatch.rationale: a master mismatch is a statement about the build, so it may punish the build

per_grant_mismatch.scope: watermark-enabled artifacts whose master is known good
per_grant_mismatch.action: one automatic re-verify, then discard the grant and re-mint with a new seed (a genuine re-fetch from zero, stated as such), then a stamping-pipeline alert and a support path
per_grant_mismatch.never: build quarantine — the build is fine and every other buyer is unaffected; quarantining would punish a vendor for our stamper

fallback.detail: a grant whose stamping failed serves master bytes and must therefore verify against the MASTER hash, not its now-stale per-grant hash
